findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The current implementation is vulnerable to path traversal attacks because it only strips the directory path using os.path.basename, but does not prevent attacks using relative paths or special characters. To fix this, we need to validate the filename to ensure it only contains allowed characters and does not contain relative path traversals. This can be achieved by checking for invalid characters and returning an error response if the filename is not valid.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks by using a whitelist approach or a library like pathlib
findings.fixed_code: filename = os.path.basename(filename); if not filename or '..' in filename or '/' in filename or '\' in filename: return 'Invalid filename'; with open(os.path.join('/var/data', filename)) as f: return f.read()

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The security group currently allows unrestricted SSH access on port 22, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, we need to restrict the ingress rule to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks. By updating the security group resource in the Terraform configuration, we can limit the exposure to only trusted sources.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks
findings.fixed_code: resource "aws_security_group" "app_sg" { ... ingress { from_port = 22 to_port = 22 protocol = "tcp" cidr_blocks = ["192.168.1.0/24"] } ... }

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging

To fix this, a parameter group needs to be created with logging enabled and assigned to the DB instance. This will allow logs to be stored and retained for a specified period.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Enable logging for the AWS DB instance by setting the parameter group and log retention period

attack_chains.title: Unrestricted SSH and Public IP
attack_chains.description: An attacker can gain initial access to the EC2 instance via unrestricted SSH, then use the public IP to establish a connection and gain access to the instance. This allows the attacker to move laterally within the network and potentially access sensitive data.
steps: Step 1: attacker gains initial access to the EC2 instance using finding ed4e06f5 (Security group allows unrestricted SSH) in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf
Step 2: attacker uses the public IP (finding 6783f55c) to establish a connection to the instance and gain access to the instance
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict SSH access to the EC2 instance by updating the security group to only allow incoming SSH connections from trusted IP addresses

attack_chains.title: Path Traversal and Unrestricted S3 Access
attack_chains.description: An attacker can use the path traversal vulnerability to access sensitive data, then use the unrestricted S3 access to exfiltrate the data. This allows the attacker to gain access to sensitive information and potentially use it for malicious purposes.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses the path traversal vulnerability (finding 49ef5499) in file src/app.py to access sensitive data
Step 2: attacker uses the unrestricted S3 access (finding 2af11b0c) to exfiltrate the sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Update the application code to fix the path traversal vulnerability and restrict S3 access to only allow necessary actions

attack_chains.title: EC2 Instance Compromise and IAM Privilege Escalation
attack_chains.description: An attacker can gain access to the EC2 instance, then use the instance's IAM role to escalate privileges and gain access to sensitive resources. This allows the attacker to move laterally within the network and potentially access sensitive data.
steps: Step 1: attacker gains access to the EC2 instance using finding ed4e06f5 (Security group allows unrestricted SSH) in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf
Step 2: attacker uses the instance's IAM role (finding 1d30627a) to escalate privileges and gain access to sensitive resources
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict SSH access to the EC2 instance and update the IAM role to only allow necessary actions
